messages.content: How do I make the text bigger on my iPhone? Everything is too small to read.

You can make the text bigger in Settings. It takes about a minute, and you can change it back anytime.

1. Open the **Settings** app.
2. Tap **Display & Brightness**.
3. Tap **Text Size**.
4. Drag the slider to the right. Stop when the text is easy to read.

If you need it even bigger, go to **Settings**, then **Accessibility**, then **Display & Text Size**, then **Larger Text**, and drag that slider. Very large text can make some buttons harder to tap, so slide it back a little if that happens.

messages.content: How do I send one text message to my three kids at the same time on my iPhone?

You can start a group text. It takes about a minute.

1. Open the **Messages** app.
2. Tap the **Compose** button (a square with a pencil) at the top.
3. Type the name of your first child and choose them. Do the same for the other two. You can also tap the **plus** button to pick them from your contacts.
4. Type your message.
5. Tap the **Send** button (the up arrow).

If a recipient is not using iMessage, the message is sent as an MMS or SMS.

To send a group MMS message on your iPhone, go to **Settings**, then **Messages**, and turn on **MMS Messaging**. If you don't see that option, contact your carrier to check whether your plan supports Group MMS Messaging.

messages.content: A man called saying he is from the IRS and that I owe money and must pay today. Is this real?

Hang up. Do not give him any personal or financial information, and do not pay.

1. Do not send money by wire transfer, prepaid card, or gift card to someone claiming to be from the IRS.
2. If you are in doubt, call the IRS directly at 1-800-829-1040.
3. Report the call to the Treasury Inspector General for Tax Administration at tigta.gov.
4. Also report it to the FTC at ftc.gov/complaint.

The IRS will not require a specific type of payment.

sources.title: FTC Consumer Advice: Those (not really) IRS calls
